L2614@P61: A VARIATIONAL BAYES ALGORITHM FOR JOINT-SPARSE ABUNDANCE ESTIMATION
L2615@P61: Paris V. Giampouras, Konstantinos E. Themelis, Athanasios A. Rontogiannis and Konstantinos D. Koutroumbas,
L2616@P61: IAASARS, National Observatory of Athens, GR-15236, Penteli, Greece
L2617@P61: Abstract : This paper presents a variational Bayesian scheme for semi-supervised unmixing on hyperspectral images
L2618@P61: that exploits the inherent spatial correlation between neighboring pixels. More specifically, a hierarchical Bayesian model that
L2619@P61: promotes a joint-sparse profile on the abundance vectors of adjacent pixels is developed and a computationally efficient variational
L2620@P61: Bayes algorithm is incorporated to perform Bayesian inference. The benefits of the proposed joint-sparse model are demonstrated
L2621@P61: via simulations on both synthetic and real data.
L2622@P61: XI. Session thu-p-b : Feature extraction, band selection and dimension reduction
L2623@P61: EVALUATION OF INTRINSIC DIMENSIONALITY METHODS USING RESIDUAL AND CHANGE-POINT ANALYSES
L2624@P61: Amin Alizadeh Naeini, Dept. of Surveying and Geomatics Eng., College of Engineering, University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran
L2625@P61: Saeid Homayouni, Department of Geography, University of Ottawa, Ottawa, Canada
L2626@P61: Mohammad Saadatseresht, Dept. of Surveying and Geomatics Eng., College of Engineering, University of Tehran, Tehran, Iran
L2627@P61: Hossein Torabzadeh, Remote Sensing Laboratories, University of Zurich, Zurich, Switzerland
L2628@P61: Abstract : The number of endmembers (NOE) in hyperspectral imagery plays an important role in image analysis applications such as classification, clustering and unmixing. Over the last years, different algorithms have been proposed to estimate
L2629@P61: the NOE. Nonetheless, each method depends on its own parameters’ values, and as a result, leads to different values for intrinsic
L2630@P61: dimensionality (ID). In this study a statistical-based method is proposed to evaluate different results of ID algorithms. In this
L2631@P61: method, the reasonable candidates of ID are selected using both residual analysis (RA) and Change-Point analysis (CPA). Different values for ID are then compared with these candidates. If these values are equal or close to these candidates they may be
L2632@P61: considered as the ID. Although the proposed method can be used for every ID method, here, the results of two new methods,
L2633@P61: namely, SML, and O-GENE-AH algorithms have been investigated on Pavia Center hyperspectral dataset.
L2634@P61: A NEW ANT COLONY OPTIMIZATION ALGORITHM BASED BAND SELECTION METHOD
L2635@P61: Xu Sun, Lina Yang, Qian Shen, Li Ni and Bing Zhang
L2636@P61: Chinese Academy of Sciences Institute of Remote Sensing and Digital Earth Beijing, China
L2637@P61: Abstract : For hyperspectral image processing, dimensionality reduction is an important step, which has direct impact
L2638@P61: on hyperspectral image classification accuracy. Unsupervised band selection is an important means of data dimensionality reduction. This paper presents an ant colony optimization (ACO) algorithm based hyperspectral image band selection method (ACOBS). First, four kinds of distance are used to measure the difference between the bands so to turn the band selection problem into
L2639@P61: a cumulative distance optimization problem. In order to solve the band selection problem, an ant colony optimization algorithm
L2640@P61: procedure is given, including the path search criteria (transition probability) and exchange rules (pheromone update). Experiments show that regardless of the Maximum Likelihood (ML) or Support Vector Machine (SVM), the ACO-BS selected band can
L2641@P61: get higher classification accuracy, cosine distance has obvious advantages among the four kinds of distance, followed by mutual
L2642@P61: information.
